what_this_is: Every specific power-loss point a vendor PRINTS for a material (as opposed to drawing the loss as a curve), with the qualifier exactly as printed (<= bound, approx typical, Max., or a bare number) and the page it is printed on. This is what a Steinmetz triple can be checked against; it is not a Steinmetz triple.
why_anchors_and_not_a_triple: Checked 2026-11-02: neither vendor prints a Steinmetz triple for a material. The Ferroxcube handbook prints a PV row of two to three points per material and draws the rest as curves; the TDK SIFERRIT material sheet for N87 prints loss only as curves and quotes a single max value on the product page. Two or three printed points cannot determine three exponents, and two of them are upper bounds rather than typical values, so a triple solved here would be arithmetic dressed up as vendor data. Hence: store the anchors, audit a triple the caller supplies, and say plainly that no triple is issued.

qualifiers.at_most: printed as <= or < - an upper bound, so a computed value BELOW it satisfies it
qualifiers.approx: printed as ~ (approximately) - a typical value, comparable in both directions
qualifiers.plain: printed as a bare number on a specification sheet - read as a typical value, no bound implied
qualifiers.max: printed as Max. - an upper bound on a part's guaranteed value

units.pv_equivalence: 1 kW/m^3 == 1 mW/cm^3, so these numbers feed the khz_t / khz_mt Steinmetz conventions unchanged
units.b: mT (peak, i.e. the amplitude, half the peak-to-peak swing)

sources.what: Ferroxcube 'Soft Ferrites and Accessories' data handbook, material specification pages
sources.anomaly: the PDF's own metadata title still says 'Ferroxcube Data Handbook 2009' while every page footer says 2013 Jul 31 - registered, not corrected

sources.what: Ferroxcube brochure 'Best in class power conversion material: 3C96, 3C98'
sources.page_note: the 8-page brochure does not carry a constant offset (pdf page 4 prints '3', pdf page 6 prints '5'), so both are recorded

sources.what: TDK product centre part page - the only place a number (rather than a curve) is printed for N87
sources.anomaly: the same page also prints '0.1 W/set (200 mT, 100 kHz, 100 C)' for one specific part; a per-set loss is not a density, so only the kW/m^3 value is carried

3C90.note: the same PV column mixes <= with ~, so these three points cannot all be fitted: a triple that hits the two bounds exactly would have to fall below the typical value

3C92.note: two points; the sheet also prints Bsat at 140 C but no loss at 140 C

3C93.note: all three points are at 140 C, the temperature this grade is specified at

3C94.note: same printed numbers as 3C92 at the same conditions - two grades, one column each

3C96.note: printed twice: this 2013 handbook row and the 2022 brochure row agree to the digit

3C98.note: the brochure's own text states 250 mW/cm^3 at 100 kHz, 200 mT, which is the same number as the 250 kW/m^3 row (1 kW/m^3 == 1 mW/cm^3)

N87.note: one max value only: the N87 SIFERRIT material data sheet (12 pages, June 2025) draws loss as three curve families and prints no numbers

3B7.note: a filter grade: the specification page prints tan delta/mu_i and DF instead of any PV row, so it has no loss anchor at all

N27.note: the product page quotes 920 kW/m^3 without stating the (B, f, T) it belongs to, so it is a quote and not an anchor; magnetic_materials.json already carries it as pv_quoted_unconditioned_kw_m3

read_method: The text stream of the handbook interleaves the PV condition column with the axis labels of the figure beside it, so every row was also re-read from word coordinates (condition column at one x, value column at another, figure labels beyond a third), and the two reads were compared; the 3C90 and 3C96 rows were additionally checked against the 2022 brochure.

3C96_printed_twice.reading: two independent printings nine years apart agree on all three points

brochure_text_against_its_own_table.reading: same number once the units are converted (1 kW/m^3 == 1 mW/cm^3)

column_shift_check.method: each material's printed grid was read as a power law (ratio at fixed f gives beta, ratio at fixed B gives alpha)

3C90.caveat: mixes a bound with a typical value, so this is a shift check and not a fit

3C93.alpha_note: the 500 kHz row breaks the power law, as it should where the fit window ends

column_shift_check.reading: implied exponents land in the range MnZn power ferrites are published in, which is what a column shift would destroy; no exponents are stored because this is not a fit
